---
title: "Happiness"
format: html
---

Every March the World Happiness Report turns well-being into a global headline — Finland is once again the happiest country in the world. This website looks behind that single number and asks a broader question: **what actually explains happiness, and what stays unexplained?**

Using World Happiness Report 2025 data (country-year life-evaluation scores and the factors behind them), we investigate two questions:

- **Q1 — What explains happiness?** Which factors — GDP, social support, health, freedom, generosity, low corruption — are most strongly associated with well-being, and do countries fall into distinct well-being profiles?
- **Q2 — What remains unexplained?** After modelling happiness from those factors, which countries are happier or less happy than the model predicts?
